articles.title: Modern robot-assisted radiosurgery of cerebral angiomas-own experiences, system comparisons, and comprehensive literature overview.
articles.abstract: Cerebral arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are rare vascular lesions potentially responsible for substantial neurological morbidity and mortality. Over the past four decades, radiosurgery has become a valid therapeutic option for many patients with small intracranial AVMs, but reports describing the use of robotic stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) are rare. The purposes of this study are to describe the efficacy and toxicity of robotic SRS for AVMs and to review the literature. The reports of 48 consecutive patients treated with SRS were reviewed. A total dose of 18 Gy in a single fraction was prescribed to the 70% isodose line. Efficacy (i.e., total obliteration of the AVM) and toxicity were analyzed. Literature search was performed on Embase and PubMed for the terms "Radiosurgery and AVMs", "Cyberknife and AVMs" and "Radiation therapy and AVMs." The median follow-up was 41 months. The median AVM volume was 2.62 cm3. The incidence of obliteration was 59% at 3 years. Regarding toxicity, 92% of patients remained symptom-free, 66% developed radiogenic edema on MRI, and none developed radionecrosis. Forty-one patients (85%) had embolization prior to SRS. Our study was incorporated in an exhaustive review of 25 trials categorized by SRS technique. In this review, the median follow-up was 60 months. The median nidus volume was 2 cm3. The median overall obliteration rate for SRS was 68% (range 36 to 92). The median embolization rate prior to SRS was 31% (range 8.23 to 90). Compared to other studies, tolerability was excellent and the obliteration rate was acceptable but probably affected by the high embolization rate prior to radiosurgery. Our study suggests that a higher dose is feasible. A larger cohort with a longer follow-up period will be needed to confirm the safety and effectiveness, and subsequently validate different prognosis and predictive scores with this treatment modality to maximize the benefits of this technology for selected patients in the long term.

articles.title: A Rare Case of Brain Angiolipoma Imitating Arteriovenous Malformation: Differential Diagnosis, Surgical Treatment, and Literature Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angiolipomas are mesenchymal tumors composed of mature adipocytes with abnormal vascular elements. They are most commonly found in subcutaneous tissues of the trunk and are rarely seen at craniospinal axes.
CASE DESCRIPTION: We present an untypical case of frontal lobe angiolipoma manifested with seizures and initially described as an arteriovenous malformation.
CONCLUSION: MRI with fat-suppression sequence plays key role in angiolipomas diagnostics.

articles.title: Stereotactic radiosurgery alone or combined with embolization for brain arteriovenous malformations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE Embolization of brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) prior to stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) has been reported to negatively affect obliteration rates. The goal of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to compare the outcomes of AVMs treated with embolization plus SRS (E+SRS group) and those of AVMs treated with SRS alone (SRS group). METHODS A literature review was performed using PubMed to identify studies with 10 or more AVM patients and obliteration data for both E+SRS and SRS groups. A meta-analysis was performed to compare obliteration rates between the E+SRS and SRS groups. RESULTS Twelve articles comprising 1716 patients were eligible for analysis. Among the patients with radiological follow-up data, complete obliteration was achieved in 48.4% of patients (330/681) in the E+SRS group compared with 62.7% of patients (613/978) in the SRS group. A meta-analysis of the pooled data revealed that the obliteration rate was significantly lower in the E+SRS group (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.41-0.64, p < 0.00001). Symptomatic adverse radiation effects were observed in 6.6% (27/412 patients) and 11.1% (48/433 patients) of the E+SRS and SRS groups, respectively. The annual post-SRS hemorrhage rate was 2.0%-6.5% and 0%-2.0% for the E+SRS and SRS groups, respectively. The rates of permanent morbidity were 0%-6.7% and 0%-13.5% for the E+SRS and SRS groups, respectively. CONCLUSIONS Arteriovenous malformation treatment with combined embolization and SRS is associated with lower obliteration rates than those with SRS treatment alone. However, this comparison does not fully account for differences in the initial AVM characteristics in the E+SRS group as compared with those in the SRS group. Further studies are warranted to address these limitations.

articles.title: Angiopoietin-Like Proteins 4 (ANGPTL4) Gene Polymorphisms and Risk of Brain Arteriovenous Malformation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain arteriovenous malformations (BAVMs) are formed by hypertrophied arterial vessels (afferents, feeders), a large number of arteriovenous shunts which become tangled to form a body (nidus) of malformation, which then expands draining proximal veins. The aim of this study was a replication of single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs11672433 association with BAVM development with the subsequent meta-analysis of published data.
METHODS: A total of 252 Russian patients with brain BAVMs and 480 control subjects were included in the present study. Genotyping was performed using real-time polymerase chain reaction with competitive hydrolysis probes.
RESULTS: In our case-control study, we found no significant association with brain arteriovenous malformation for the SNP rs11672433 of ANGPTL4 gene (odds ratio .82, 95% confidence interval = .57-1.17 P value = .27) as well as in meta-analysis (odds ratio 1.18, 95% confidence interval = .81-1.73, P value = .39).
CONCLUSIONS: Our data showed that SNP rs11672433 was not associated with the BAVM Russian population and the following meta-analysis did not detect an association in total. Thus, in spite of the fact that ANGPTL4 (protein) participates in the angiogenesis regulation processes, we consider that SNP rs11672433, a high-frequency locus in the ANGPTL4 gene, does not influence the predisposition to BAVM or its effect is too small to be detected in the present size sample set.

articles.title: [Abernethy Malformation - Congenital Portosystemic Shunts and the Transition Toward Minimally Invasive Therapy].
articles.abstract: Congenital portosystemic shunts (CPSS), also known as Abernethy malformation, are rare congenital vascular anomalies of the portal venous circulation. In this condition, blood from the abdominal organs is completely or partially diverted past the liver. Depending on its extent and location, the shunt can have various clinical consequences. In addition to asymptomatic courses, severe metabolic, neurological, or pulmonary complications have also been described. Modern imaging techniques such as duplex sonography, magnetic resonance imaging, and catheter angiography now allow for a much more accurate assessment of the shunt. Much has also changed in terms of treatment. Whereas liver transplantation used to be the only curative option for severe shunts the focus today is on often sequential closure of the shunt. In most cases physiological portal venous blood flow can be restored using interventional or surgical, minimally invasive procedures. In selected cases, shunt closure may be associated with the development of portal hypertension due to hypoplastic portal venous structures. This article summarizes current findings on the development, diagnosis, and treatment of this condition.

articles.title: Therapeutic Apheresis in Nigeria: Awareness, Knowledge Gaps, and Readiness for Service Expansion Among Healthcare Professionals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic apheresis (TA) is a specialized extracorporeal blood purification modality used in the management of complex hematologic, neurologic, and autoimmune diseases. Despite established global guidelines, its utilization in Nigeria remains largely undocumented. This study assessed awareness, technical knowledge, and institutional readiness for TA among Nigerian healthcare professionals.
METHODS: We conducted an open, cross-sectional online survey of licensed Nigerian healthcare professionals, recruited by convenience and snowball sampling through professional social media networks (WhatsApp, Instagram, X) over a 2-month period from January 29, 2026, to April 1, 2026. Because recruitment used an open, non-probability sampling frame, a conventional response rate could not be calculated; of 180 questionnaires received, 155 (86.1%) met pre-specified completeness and uniqueness criteria and were analyzed. The questionnaire assessed demographics, awareness of TA services, technical knowledge (10-item assessment based on ASFA guideline domains), and perceived barriers.
RESULTS: Respondents were predominantly physicians (63.2%; consultants 22.6%, residents 40.6%), practicing mainly in teaching (47.7%) and private (32.9%) hospitals; 51.6% practiced in a single state (Imo State). Awareness of TPE centers was moderate (45.2%, 95% CI: 37.6%-53.1%), and clinical exposure was low (27.7%, 95% CI: 21.3%-35.2%). The mean knowledge score was 5.10 ± 2.44 of 10. Knowledge level was not significantly associated with professional role, years of experience, or institution type (all p > 0.05), with a borderline, nonsignificant difference by specialty (p = 0.051); nephrology and critical care specialists showed the highest proportion of good knowledge. The leading perceived barriers were lack of equipment (79.4%), poor funding (75.5%), limited awareness (75.5%), and lack of trained personnel (74.2%). Nearly all respondents (95.5%) supported establishing a national TA registry.
CONCLUSION: Nigerian healthcare professionals report substantial gaps in TA awareness and technical knowledge alongside strong readiness to support service expansion. These findings, drawn predominantly from a single geopolitical zone, support targeted investment in structured training, equipment and reimbursement pathways, and a coordinated national apheresis registry, while highlighting the need for confirmatory studies with broader geographic and professional representation.

articles.title: Dengue virus infection and Guillain-Barré syndrome: a systematic review of clinical characteristics, outcomes, and predictors of severity.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus causing significant morbidity in tropical and subtropical regions. While not classically neurotropic, DENV has been increasingly associated with neurological complications, including Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS). This review synthesizes evidence on epidemiology, clinical features, outcomes, and predictors of severity in dengue-associated GBS. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed and Embase (April 2025) using terms for dengue and GBS. Eligible studies were case reports/series with individual-level data on laboratory-confirmed or clinically diagnosed dengue preceding GBS. RESULTS: Thirty-six publications describing 56 patients from Asia, Latin America, and other endemic regions were included. The mean age was 34.9 years (range 1.5–73), with 57% male. 95% had symptomatic dengue; thrombocytopenia occurred in 43%. Median latency from dengue onset to GBS was 7 days. Motor weakness was universal; facial palsy (32%), bulbar weakness (28.6%), sensory deficits (33.9%), and autonomic dysfunction (18%) were common. Electrophysiology showed AMSAN (33.9%), AIDP (32.1%), and AMAN (12.5%). Albuminocytologic dissociation was present in 62.5% of CSF samples. IVIG was administered in 76.7%, plasmapheresis in 14.3%; 25% required mechanical ventilation. Outcomes were favorable in most: 57% achieved full recovery, 32% partial recovery, and 5.4% mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Dengue-associated GBS resembles other post-infectious forms but shows a high proportion of axonal subtypes. Prognosis is generally good with standard therapy. Although severe cases, particularly those with thrombocytopenia, are more likely to require ICU care. Clinicians in endemic areas should maintain a high index of suspicion for GBS in the post-dengue period to enable timely diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Effects of different therapeutic methods on the 90-day prognosis of patients with HBV-ACLF: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The short-term mortality rate of hepatitis B virus related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF) is relatively high, and the optimal therapeutic method for HBV-ACLF is still controversial. This study aimed to investigate the effects of different therapeutic methods on 90-day prognosis of HBV-ACLF patients.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched from their inception date up to February 2, 2023. RCTs or cohort studies related to the treatment of HBV-ACLF with different therapies were identified. Therapeutic methods focused on plasma exchange (PE), mesenchymal stem cell (MSC), granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF), glucocorticoid (GC), double plasma molecular absorption system (DPMAS), and nucleos(t)ide analogues. The primary outcome was the 90-day survival rate. The results for binary variables were calculated using odds ratio (OR), with a corresponding 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: A total of 16 studies were included in this study, which contained the therapeutic methods of PE, GC, G-CSF, MSC, DPMAS + PE, MSC + PE. Compared to nucleos(t)ide analogues, treatment with MSC + PE, DPMAS + PE, G-CSF, MSC and PE increased the odds of 90-day survival rate (OR = 4.58, 95% CI: 1.95-10.75; OR = 2.95, 95% CI: 1.07-8.12; OR = 2.32, 95% CI: 1.15-4.69; OR = 2.36, 95% CI: 1.14-4.91; OR = 1.91, 95% CI: 1.42-2.77), respectively. The odds of the 90-day survival rate after being treated by MSC + PE were superior to PE (OR = 2.40, 95% CI: 1.05-5.51) and GC treatment (OR = 2.86, 95% CI: 1.01-8.09). MSC + PE exhibited the highest likelihood (0.92) of being the optimal therapeutic method in improving the prognosis of patients with HBV-ACLF. For single-drug regimens, G-CSF (0.58) ranks the highest.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis showed that MSC + PE was the most effective therapy in improving the 90-day prognosis, and G-CSF was the potential optimal monotherapy in improving the 90-day prognosis of HBV-ACLF patients.

articles.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus in critical care: A systematic review of ICU outcomes and management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) often progresses to critical illness requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission, yet contemporary data on outcomes, prognostic factors, and therapeutic approaches are scattered.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize recent evidence on causes of ICU admission, mortality predictors, and management strategies in adult SLE.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant search of PubMed, Web of Science and Cochrane Library (inception-31 December 2024) retrieved studies enrolling adults (≥18 years) with confirmed SLE treated in ICUs. Two reviewers independently selected articles and extracted data; methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis, so results were narratively synthesized.
RESULTS: Thirty-nine studies met the criteria. Infection (40 %), pulmonary involvement (17 %) and renal flares (13 %) were the most common admission triggers. Reported ICU mortality ranged from 20 % to 82 % but rose sharply when baseline Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K) exceeded 16, approximating 80 % mortality (sensitivity 84 %, specificity 90 %) and outperforming Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) II and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) in discriminating survivors. Additional independent predictors were APACHE II > 16, need for mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy and vasopressor support. Mechanical ventilation (59 %) and vasoactive agents (39 %) were the predominant ICU interventions. Immunomodulatory management was heterogeneous: high-dose corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide were ubiquitous, whereas mycophenolate, antimalarials, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasmapheresis, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation were reserved for selected scenarios.
CONCLUSIONS: Early recognition of poor prognostic factors and prompt ICU admission are essential to improving outcomes in SLE.

articles.title: RBM47-Mediated Stabilization of PARP1 mRNA Exacerbates Subarachnoid Hemorrhage With RBM47 Transcriptionally Regulated by EGR1.
articles.abstract: Early brain injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is chiefly marked by neuronal apoptosis and neuroinflammation, while the principal regulating molecules have yet to be identified. RBM47 exhibited considerable upregulation in the cerebral cortex of SAH mice and hemoglobin (Hb)-induced primary cortical neurons. Knockdown of RBM47 with intracerebroventricular injection of small interfering RNA improved neurobehavioral scores (modified Garcia score and beam balance test), mitigated brain edema and SAH grade, and decreased the quantity of FJC-positive and TUNEL-positive neurons in the cortex. Furthermore, RBM47 knockdown suppressed the expression of apoptotic proteins, obstructed HMGB1 nuclear to cytoplasmic translocation, and reduced TNF-α and IL-6 concentrations. In vitro results further validated that RBM47 knockdown diminished Hb-induced neuronal apoptosis and neuroinflammation. The transcription factor EGR1 directly bound to the RBM47 promoter and transcriptionally stimulated RBM47. RBM47 enhanced PARP1 expression by binding to the 3'UTR of PARP1 mRNA. Co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated a connection between PARP1 and HMGB1, facilitating HMGB1 release. We conducted label-free proteomics analysis on primary neurons following PARP1 knockdown and Hb therapy. Differentially expressed proteins were enriched in ADP ribosylation, regulation of necroptosis, and the extrinsic apoptotic pathway. GSEA revealed a large negative enrichment of the neuronal apoptotic process, while pathways associated with mitochondrial activity exhibited highly significant positive enrichment. EGR1 transcriptionally stimulates RBM47, which then enhances HMGB1 release by upregulating PARP1, therefore facilitating neuronal death and inflammation following SAH. PARP1 knockdown alters the mitochondrial protein expression profile and inhibits apoptosis and necroptosis. Targeting the EGR1/RBM47/PARP1/HMGB1 axis may provide an innovative therapeutic approach for SAH.

articles.title: Multi-Organ Inflammatory and Endocrine Crosstalk Shapes the Early Brain Response to Combined Burn and Blast Injury.
articles.abstract: The pathology of concomitant burn and traumatic brain injury remains poorly defined, despite their frequent co-occurrence in military settings and the potential for deleterious synergy. To address this gap, we combined established models of blast-induced mild traumatic brain injury and 15% total body surface area flame burn to approximate a common combat-related trauma and examined how the injuries interact to shape systemic inflammation and brain transcriptional programs. Burn injury induced systemic G-CSF and IL-6 secretion and hematopoietic reprioritization, whereas overlapping brain injury did not substantially alter these systemic effects but magnified brain transcriptional responses relative to single injuries. Bulk RNA-seq profiling at 6 h post-injury revealed enriched gene sets associated with inflammation and endocrine stress in the combined injury group, alongside elevated systemic cytokines and corticosterone; thereby suggesting concurrent immune-endocrine activation. Since our prior work demonstrated burn wound-associated IL-1 signaling induces G-CSF and IL-6 secretion, we tested IL-1 neutralizing antibodies and anakinra as therapies. Treatment reduced G-CSF and IL-6 secretion, improved erythropoiesis, and selectively modulated brain transcriptional changes. Single-nucleus RNA-seq projection mapping predicted that the transcripts altered by combined injury were broadly enriched across vascular and glial cell types. Targeted expression profiling identified a shared brain-liver signature characterized by an IL-1/6-dependent inflammatory response alongside an interleukin-independent stress response. These findings highlight IL-1-responsive inflammatory signals and endocrine stress interactions within a multi-organ network that shapes the early brain transcriptional response to the combined injury.

articles.title: Argatroban mitigates Klebsiella pneumoniae liver injury by attenuating ZBP1-dependent PANoptosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) liver abscess (KPLA) is frequently accompanied by thrombophlebitis and systemic inflammation. Argatroban, a direct thrombin inhibitor, has anti-inflammatory potential, but its efficacy and mechanism in KPLA remain unclear.
METHODS: A murine KPLA model was established using a hypervirulent, patient-derived K. pneumoniae strain, with mice receiving vehicle or argatroban (10 mg kg-1/day, i.p.). Survival, liver pathology, vascular permeability, inflammatory responses, and transcriptomic changes were evaluated. Hepatocyte responses were investigated using KP-LPS-stimulated THLE-2 cells. ZBP1 localization, protein interactions, and functional dependence were assessed by immunofluorescence, co-immunoprecipitation, and ZBP1 silencing.
RESULTS: Argatroban significantly improved 72-h survival (P = 0.02), reduced hepatic necrosis, attenuated sinusoidal vascular leakage, and suppressed systemic inflammatory cytokine production in KPLA mice. RNA-seq revealed activation of innate immune-sensing pathways during infection, which were markedly attenuated by argatroban. ZBP1 and PANoptosis-associated molecules were increased in KPLA livers and reduced by argatroban. ZBP1 was predominantly localized in hepatocytes. In KP-LPS-stimulated THLE-2 cells, RIPK3, ASC, and Caspase-8 showed enhanced intracellular co-localization, while co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated ZBP1 interactions with RIPK3, ASC, and Caspase-8. ZBP1 silencing markedly reduced KP-LPS-induced activation of p-MLKL, cleaved GSDMD, and cleaved caspase-3, supporting ZBP1-dependent PANoptosis as a key driver of hepatocyte inflammatory injury. Mechanistically, argatroban inhibited TLR4 endocytosis and downstream TBK1/IRF3-STAT1 signaling, thereby suppressing ZBP1 induction.
CONCLUSIONS: Argatroban protects against KPLA-associated liver injury by inhibiting a TLR4 endocytosis-TBK1/IRF3-STAT1-ZBP1 axis and suppressing ZBP1-dependent PANoptosis, identifying PANoptosis as a potential therapeutic target in severe K. pneumoniae infection.

articles.title: Proton Radiotherapy Offers Immune-Sparing Benefits in Glioblastoma Treatment.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Glioblastoma (GB) and x-ray-based radiation therapy are associated with lymphopenia, which worsens prognosis and impairs antitumor immunity. Proton therapy, with its dosimetric properties that spare healthy brain tissue, is an alternative to reduce radiotoxicity. This study examined the effects of brain irradiation with x-rays or protons on lymphopenia.
METHODS AND MATERIALS: We used GL261-tumor-bearing and tumor-free mice models to evaluate various lymphoid and myeloid cell populations after brain irradiation, assessing volume of brain irradiation, beam orientation, and lymphopenia onset timing via flow cytometry.
RESULTS: In the GB mouse model, both tumor- and radiation-induced lymphopenia were evidenced. Severe lymphopenia, with a 50% depletion of CD45+CD3+ lymphocytes, CD3+CD4+ and CD3+CD8+ T-cell, CD3-B220+ B cells, and CD45+CD11b+ myeloids, CD11b+Ly6C+ monocytes, and CD11b+Ly6G+ neutrophils, occurred as early as 12 hours after x-ray exposure in tumor-free mice. Myeloid subtypes recovered by day 2, whereas lymphocyte recovery was cell type dependent. The use of a lateral x-ray beam failed to alter circulating lymphocyte counts. Brain, cervical lymph nodes, and spleen immune cell quantification revealed a reduction in CD3+CD4+, CD3+CD8+ T and CD3-B220+ B cells post-x-ray exposure. Protons caused a 15% decrease in circulating lymphocytes, with no change in myeloid cells. Proton exposure also reduced CD3+CD4+ T and CD3-B220+ B cells in the cervical lymph nodes but did not affect the spleen. Plasma cytokine levels in the interleukin 1 and macrophage inflammatory protein families correlated with leucocyte changes following exposure to both particle types.
CONCLUSIONS: We describe that proton therapy resulted in less lymphopenia than proton radiation, and propose that the mechanism may be related to biological processes rather than solely decreased exposure of circulating lymphocytes. This may be used to guide the incorporation of immune therapy in GB.
SYNOPSIS: Understanding how brain irradiation affects circulating immunity can inform strategies to improve brain tumor treatment. This involves combining irradiation with immunotherapy and adjusting clinical protocols to restore lymphocytes/boost antitumor T cells.

articles.title: Baicalin-Enhanced Microglial Repopulation Suppresses NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation and Promotes Neuroprotection in an LPS-Induced Mouse Model.
articles.abstract: Microglia are the primary innate immune cells in the brain, essential under physiological conditions for maintaining homeostasis. Chronic activation of microglia is associated with the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway, especially following exposure to lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Microglia can be eliminated using a CSF1R inhibitor such as BLZ945. However, NLRP3 inflammasome markers (NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, IL-1β, and TNF-α) show increased expression following repopulation. This indicates a persistent inflammatory response. To address this, we orally administered a flavonoid compound baicalin which was extracted from the plant Scutellaria baicalensis, to mice during the microglial repopulation phase. Baicalin restored microglial homeostasis and suppressed NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Improved behavioral outcomes and reduced oxidative stress as a result of baicalin were observed at the molecular level. This study investigated whether microglial depletion with BLZ945 followed by baicalin administration promotes microglial repopulation and reduces neuroinflammation compared to BLZ945 treatment alone. Taken together, this suggests that adjusting microglial repopulation may give a wider window to control neuroinflammation. This suggests that baicalin works alongside BLZ945 to improve neuroprotection, particularly in situations where BLZ945 alone is not enough. Overall, baicalin shows potential as a modulator in chronic neuroinflammatory conditions and may be worth exploring in future research.

articles.title: CD14 in glioblastoma and temozolomide resistance: what the evidence does and does not support.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM), designated as central nervous system World Health Organization grade 4, is the most lethal adult brain tumor, with a median overall survival (OS) of 14.6 months despite resection, radiotherapy, and temozolomide (TMZ). The benefit of TMZ is largely confined to the 45 % of GBMs carrying a methylated O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter, where, in 206 assessable patients from the pivotal Phase III trial (reported in 2005), adding TMZ to radiotherapy extended median OS from 15.3 to 21.7 months, whereas MGMT-unmethylated tumors derived no significant benefit; these are historical estimates from a single trial subset. Resistance arises through MGMT-mediated repair of O6-methylguanine, MSH6 loss or mutation affecting mismatch repair, glioma stem cell repopulation, and an immunosuppressive microenvironment enriched with CD14+ myeloid cells, including tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), monocytes, and monocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells. CD14 is a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored co-receptor for Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), expressed constitutively on monocytes, macrophages, and microglia and also by a subset of glioma cells. Because CD14 has no intracellular domain, it cannot signal independently of a partner receptor; CD14-dependent signaling through TLR4/MD-2 has been proposed to contribute to nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activation, pro-survival transcription, MGMT-related resistance pathways, and immunosuppressive myeloid polarization, although no study has shown this in glioma cells, the link to TMZ resistance remains hypothetical, and CD14 alone does not define an M2-like TAM phenotype. This review synthesizes over 50 publications across CD14 biology in the brain, CD14 expression across the immune and tumor-cell landscape of GBM, CD14-associated inflammatory signaling, TMZ resistance mechanisms, CD14-related influences on TMZ sensitivity, and candidate therapeutic strategies. Of those strategies, only IC14 (atibuclimab) targets CD14 directly; TLR4, NF-κB, signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 and colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor inhibition, TAM repolarization, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibition, and checkpoint blockade act on the partner receptor, on shared downstream nodes or on the CD14-enriched myeloid compartment, and are therefore described as CD14-associated rather than CD14-targeted. CD14+ myeloid populations are associated with aggressive GBM biology, whereas the proposed glioma-cell-intrinsic CD14 → TLR4/MD-2 → NF-κB → MGMT cascade rests on a single 2003 expression dataset and has never been tested by CD14 loss-of-function, gain-of-function, rescue or lineage-specific in vivo experiments. The purpose of this review is to document that gap and to specify the experiments that would close it, not to advocate CD14 as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Forward programming of human pluripotent stem cells to endothelial cells utilizing ETV2-mRNA delivery with ionizable lipid nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) represent a scalable source of cells for off-the-shelf therapeutics and advanced in vitro tissue models. However, their translational utility is constrained by inefficient differentiation protocols that rely on small molecules, cytokines, or genomic modification. Here, we describe a non-integrating approach that utilizes ionizable lipid nanoparticles (iLNPs) to deliver mRNA encoding the ETV2 transcription factor to efficiently forward reprogram hPSCs to endothelial cells (ECs). This platform achieved transfection efficiencies exceeding 97%, with robust expression of functional mRNA cargo. ETV2 delivery induced rapid endothelial conversion, generating cell populations with average purities greater than 90% based on expression of canonical endothelial surface markers Pecam-1 (CD31) and VE-Cadherin (CD144). Forward programming efficiency depended upon culture parameters including initial seeding density, mRNA dosage, and time after transfection. Functionally, iLNP-ETV2-derived ECs exhibited hallmark endothelial behaviors, including angiogenic network formation in vitro, uptake of acetylated low-density lipoprotein, and inflammatory cytokine responsiveness. Collectively, these findings establish iLNP-mediated ETV2 mRNA delivery as an efficient and non-genome-integrating strategy for forward programming hPSCs to ECs, facilitating their use in tissue engineering, disease modeling, and cell-based therapy applications. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Human pluripotent stem cells are a promising source of cells for regenerative medicine and tissue engineering, but existing differentiation methods often produce low yields and require extensive optimization. In this study, we demonstrate that ionizable lipid nanoparticles can achieve highly efficient mRNA delivery to pluripotent stem cells and enable efficient, non-integrating forward programming to endothelial cells through transient expression of the transcription factor ETV2. This approach generated highly pure endothelial populations that retained key endothelial functions and remained stable during long-term expansion. Importantly, endothelial conversion was maintained across broad ranges of cell seeding densities and mRNA doses, suggesting a robust and scalable manufacturing process. These findings establish a versatile platform for mRNA based cell engineering and stem cell differentiation.

articles.title: Research Progress of Low-Intensity Pulsed Ultrasound in Parkinson's Disease.
articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder where current pharmacological and surgical interventions, including Deep Brain Stimulation, often fail to reverse neuronal degeneration or halt disease progression. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) has emerged as a novel, non-invasive neuromodulation technology with significant therapeutic potential. This review synthesizes current research on the key acoustic parameters, biological mechanisms, and clinical applications of LIPUS in PD. Unlike High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU), which relies on thermal ablation to destroy target nuclei (e.g., Vim, STN), LIPUS utilizes low-energy mechanical waves (typically <3 W/cm²) to exert non-thermal regulatory effects without damaging tissue. Mechanisms of action include the modulation of mechanosensitive ion channels (e.g., Piezo1), enhancement of neuroplasticity via brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), promotion of autophagy, and regulation of microglial phenotypes to reduce neuroinflammation. We further compare LIPUS with HIFU, highlighting the superiority of LIPUS regarding safety, reversibility, and the absence of requirement for MRI-based thermal monitoring. While preliminary clinical studies using wearable LIPUS devices indicate improvements in motor and cognitive functions, a unified consensus on optimal stimulation parameters and targeting strategies is lacking. Future research should focus on large-scale, standardized clinical trials to establish precise protocols for LIPUS as a disease-modifying therapy for PD.

articles.title: CD4+ T cells are required for tumor antigen-expressing oHSV glioma therapeutic effect and antigen-specific antibody production.
articles.abstract: Malignant gliomas are treatment-resistant brain tumors needing new therapies. Virotherapy is an experimental therapy that uses attenuated viruses that conditionally replicate and lyse tumor cells and induce tumor immune therapeutic activity. How oncolytic viruses coordinate different arms of the adaptive immune response and mediate glioma therapeutic efficacy remains incompletely defined. We previously showed that an oncolytic virus expressing a shared tumor antigen, ephrin type-A receptor 2 (EphA2), created EphA2-reactive CD8+ T cell formation. Here, we show that, in addition to this CD8+ response, EphA2-oncolytic herpes simplex virus (oHSV) (C170) elicits a coordinated CD4+ T cell and B cell response with functional capacity contributing to glioma control. C170 promotes a T helper type 1 (Th1) and IL-21+CD4+ T cell population, dendritic cell (DC) activation, and germinal center B cell expansion in the tumor draining lymph nodes and produces activated B cell glioma infiltrates with enhanced antigen-presenting capacity. Depletion studies show that C170 therapeutic activity requires CD4+ T cells and that their loss reduces EphA2-specific antibody production. C170-treated mouse serum has improved complement-dependent cytotoxicity in vitro and can suppress tumor growth in vivo. These findings show that antigen-expressing oncolytic virotherapy induces a CD4+ T cell-dependent tumor therapeutic effect and generates a functional tumor antigen-specific humoral response, providing another potential mechanism contributing to C170 therapeutic efficacy.

articles.title: Hypoxic bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes promote neurovascular repair in ischemic stroke with CXCR4-Associated enhancement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and mortality worldwide, with limited therapeutic options for long-term recovery. Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC)-derived exosomes have emerged as a promising cell-free therapy, but their efficacy is often constrained by poor homing efficiency.
METHODS: Hypoxic preconditioning and silencing CXCR4 was done through genetic modification of rat BMSCs. The exosomes were captured and identified through transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking and western blot. The middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model was established and animals were treated with exosomes derived from normoxic, hypoxic, and CXCR4-ooverexpressed or knock-downed BMSCs. Neurological function, infarct volume, vascular density, apoptosis, and neuroinflammation were assessed through behavioral tests, TTC staining, immunofluorescence, and TUNEL assays.
RESULTS: Hypoxic preconditioning significantly enhanced the therapeutic effects of BMSC-derived exosomes, as evidenced by improved neurological scores, reduced infarct volume, and increased cerebral microvascular perfusion. CXCR4 overexpression further enhanced these hypoxia-associated benefits, whereas CXCR4 knockdown partially attenuated them, suggesting that CXCR4 contributes to the therapeutic effects of hypoxic BMSC-derived exosomes.
CONCLUSION: Hypoxic BMSC-derived exosomes promote neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke, and CXCR4 appears to be an important contributing factor that enhances these therapeutic effects.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance imaging of congenital brain malformations.
articles.abstract: Congenital brain malformations can contribute to significant morbidity and mortality. Severity and prognosis depend on the character, extent, and anatomical localization as well as associated genetic syndromes and other organ system involvement. Correct diagnosis is crucial for early interventions including supportive therapies, prognostic and genetic counseling, medical management, and/or surgical correction. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) improves early diagnosis and prognostication. This review outlines clinical signs and symptoms that may warrant an MRI followed by an overview of various cerebral, posterior fossa, and vascular malformations, as well as corpus callosum abnormalities with representative MR images as well as recommendations on how to set up and optimally perform MRI. Lastly, this review presents perspectives and focus areas for further research. IMPACT: What is the key message of your article? Magnetic resonance imaging is a key component to the diagnosis and prognosis of congenital brain malformations. What does it add to the existing literature? This review provides an updated review on the current literature on congenital brain malformations as well as recommendations for integrating MRI into clinical practice. What is the impact? This review contributes with recommendations on what to expect when interpreting MR images of neonates with suspected congenital brain malformations.
